payload.opinion:
GRANTED IN PART, REFUSED IN PART. Blue is right about the facts, right about the
principle, and partly wrong about the relief. I set out what I verified myself,
what I hold, what binds whom, and — because it matters more than the holding —
the limits of what I am actually able to make bind.

I. WHAT I VERIFIED, DIRECTLY, AND WITH WHAT

I did not take blue's filing on trust. Every factual assertion in it was
re-checked against the artifact and the record before I ruled.

1. blue/report.md in this run is 176 bytes. It is one line of text plus a
   trailing newline: the H1 title, and nothing else. `grep -n '^##'` against it
   exits 1 — there is no `## ` heading of any kind in the file, and no prose
   under any heading, because there is no prose. Blue's description ("two lines,
   line 2 empty") is accurate to the byte.

2. Red minted R1-1, R1-2 and R1-3 at 2026-08-10T04:12:02Z (records/events-red-
   merge-r1-ffebea46.jsonl, seq 1-3). I read the three mint payloads in full.
   Their `location` fields are "## TL;DR — the opening sentence", "## The
   migration's failure mode is louder", and "## The retirement test is
   unobservable". None of those sections exists in the artifact those gaps are
   filed against. R1-1 and R1-2 carry `existence: verified`; R1-3 carries
   `existence: suspected`. All three carry `fix_basis: proposed`, which is itself
   consistent with anticipation: the tool derives `verified` fix_basis only from
   a `--fix-old`/`--fix-new` pair that it validates against the live report, and
   no such pair was offered, so nothing in the mint path ever compared red's
   words to blue's bytes.

3. I checked blue's innocent explanations myself rather than accepting its
   check. blue/candidates/ exists and is empty. The sibling run
   research/2026-08-10_dual-read-vs-migration holds a 26,211-byte report on a
   near-identical question; its headings are TL;DR, The Catechism, Technical
   Foundations, Analysis, Risk Matrix, Open Questions, Bibliography. I read its
   TL;DR and Catechism. R1-2's and R1-3's locations do not exist there. R1-1's
   location partially resolves — there is a `## TL;DR` — but that TL;DR asserts
   nothing about every consumer calling a combined reader; its opening sentence
   is about tool lifetimes and organizational capacity. So the gaps were not
   audited against this run's report, and they were not audited against the
   neighbouring one either. Blue's diligence here was real and its statement of
   the result was appropriately careful.

4. I verified the meaning of the stamp against statute rather than against
   either party's characterization of it. The axis is defined in the tool's own
   enum table (tools/internal/record/enums.go, the `existence` entry): "verified
   (you checked the defect at the leaf) | suspected (inferred)", with the
   recorded rationale that grading v2 split existence from consequence precisely
   so that likelihood grades the consequence only and this field carries whether
   the defect was checked at all — "a gap whose existence is unreadable is one
   whose grades cannot be interpreted". The report renderer says the same thing
   to the eventual human reader in so many words (tools/internal/report/
   assemble.go, existenceNote): verified renders as "red checked this defect at
   the leaf". Blue's reading of the axis is the statute's reading. There is no
   second construction available on which "verified" could mean "I am confident
   in this critique".

5. I verified that blue had no ordinary channel. `blue dispute --dimension`
   accepts severity, likelihood, impact, complexity_cost, and nothing else. The
   one axis blue could demonstrate to be unsupported is the one axis blue has no
   verb to contest. Blue was not forum-shopping; the petition was the only door.

II. THE HOLDING, AND THE PRINCIPLE IT RESTS ON

A verification stamp is not a grade. Grades are opinions about magnitude and two
seats may honourably disagree about them forever; that is what the dispute
channel is for. `existence: verified` is a different kind of claim — it is an
assertion that an act occurred, that a seat looked at the artifact and saw the
defect there. It is the one field on a gap that is not argument. Its whole value
to a later reader is that it cannot be produced by conviction, only by looking.

On this record it was produced by conviction. I do not find bad faith and I am
not asked to: red was dispatched to audit before any drafting sitting had run,
the constitution it works under says nothing whatever about this field (the word
"existence" does not appear in red-auditor.md), and the honest reading is the one
blue offered — the field was filled with confidence in the critique rather than
confirmation of the text. That is a category error. But a category error in the
one field that certifies looking is not a clerical matter, because its
consequence is exactly the failure this repository has named and measured: the
absent case and the healthy case become the same bytes. A gap red predicted and a
gap red confirmed render identically to every downstream reader, and the reader
has no way to tell which one this was. The mint path cannot refuse it, because
`--location` is free prose validated against nothing; only the fix-pair is
checked against the live report, and no fix-pair was offered.

The values in tension are adversarial latitude against evidentiary integrity.
Red's latitude to anticipate is worth protecting and I protect it below —
pre-motion critique aimed at a report not yet written is a legitimate and
probably useful practice, and blue said so itself and asked me not to disturb it.
But latitude to predict is not latitude to certify. Integrity wins here, and it
wins narrowly: the practice survives, the stamp does not.

III. WHAT I GRANT

(b) is GRANTED, in modified form, and it is the operative part.

R1-1, R1-2 and R1-3 are ANTICIPATORY gaps. They were minted against an artifact
containing no text they could describe, and the record now says so. Their
acceptance checks are scored against the text blue actually writes, at the first
sitting after blue has drafted, and against nothing else. No FAIL, no adverse
inference, and no grade may be banked against blue on account of the state of the
artifact at 2026-08-10T04:12:02Z. Blue's obligation in the coming round is to
draft the report; it is not to defend, rebut, or repair text that does not exist,
and it is not to write a section merely because a `location` field names one.

(a) is GRANTED AS A DECLARATION ONLY, and I want the limit stated plainly rather
than buried. I hold that the `existence: verified` stamps on R1-1 and R1-2 are
UNSUPPORTED on this record, and that every downstream reader — seats, capture,
assembly, and the human — must read those two gaps as `suspected`, inferred and
not confirmed at the leaf. I cannot make the field itself say that. There is no
verb: `merge regrade` moves severity, likelihood, impact and complexity_cost, and
those four only (I read the command's flag set); nothing in any seat's vocabulary
amends `existence` on an existing mint. So the correction lives in this opinion,
as prose, while the field it corrects goes on rendering "red checked this defect
at the leaf" to anyone who reads the board without reading me. I am obliged to
notice that this is the same defect I am ruling against, one level up: the
authoritative fact now lives in a document standing in for a record. I record it
as friction rather than pretending the ruling cured it.

(c) is GRANTED AS A DIRECTION TO RED, with a caveat I am obliged to state.

Red's next sitting should either re-anchor all three locations against blue's
drafted text — reading it first — or restate them as topic-level anticipations
whose location field claims no section. Where red wants a corrected existence
stamp on the record as a field rather than as my prose, the available mechanical
route is `merge close --as amends_prior --successor <new id>` followed by
`merge mint --supersedes <old id> --existence suspected`; that is red's call to
make, not mine to order, and I note it costs a supersedes chain for what should
have been a one-field correction.

The caveat: I checked whether a granted relief reaches red, and it does not.
Relief is threaded into the coming round's prompts at exactly one site
(debate.js line 864, the blue-response prompt); red's prompts never receive it,
and the petition log that survives to capture carries only petitioner, class and
ruling — not the opinion. Nor does a `petition-rule` event render into the
`--view debate` transcript: the debate view's `### LEAD` block is built from
`opinion` events alone. So a direction from the bench to red about red's own
conduct has no carrier at all in this machinery. I state the direction because it
is right and because the record should show it was given; I do not pretend it
binds the way (b) binds.

IV. WHAT I REFUSE, AND WHY

I refuse the conditional in blue's (b) — "may not be scored against blue until
red re-anchors it to a real span after blue drafts." That condition hands blue an
indefinite suspension of three acceptance checks in exchange for red's inaction,
and an unaudited PASS is the same wrong as an unearned FAIL, only pointed the
other way. It is also unnecessary: all three checks as written are scoreable
against whatever blue produces without reference to any location. "The report
names an enforcement mechanism, and that mechanism exists in the tree" does not
need a section heading to be run. "The section that raises the counter-argument
also disposes of it" is a claim about blue's finished prose. "The universal is
either bounded or defended" likewise. The mislocated gaps are not unscoreable;
they were merely premature. So the non-preclusion I grant is retrospective — it
reaches the empty artifact and stops there — and red's failure to re-anchor does
not suspend a check blue can be measured against once the text exists.

I also refuse, though blue did not ask for it and deserves credit for not asking:
any strike, any grade movement, and any adverse finding against red. Blue
disclaimed all three explicitly and argued the grades separately on their merits,
which is the reason this petition reads as an integrity filing rather than as a
tactic. That restraint is the reason it succeeded.

One correction against the petitioner, because a claim the record does not
support counts against the side that made it even when that side wins. Blue wrote
that the misstamp is "indistinguishable, to every later reader and to the capture
audit, from a gap red actually confirmed." I looked for the audit. There is none.
`existence` has no mechanical consumer anywhere in the tool: it is carried in the
board projection, rendered as a note in the assembled report, and read by humans
and seats. Nothing scores it, nothing gates on it, and mass and the verdict are
computed without it. The harm blue names is real but it is entirely a harm to
readers, which is a weaker and more precise claim than the one blue made. I note
it because blue's own standard this sitting was to verify at the leaf before
asserting, and on this one clause it asserted a mechanism it had not found.

V. STATUS OF THIS HOLDING

Persuasive only. law/precedents.md in this run's inputs is empty at founding;
neither party cited precedent and there is none to address. Nothing here binds a
future sitting unless a human promotes it. The rule I would offer for promotion,
stated so it can be contested: *a verification stamp certifies an act of looking
and may never be set from confidence in the critique; a gap minted against text
that does not yet exist is anticipatory, is stamped suspected, and carries no
adverse inference against the drafting seat for the state of the artifact at the
time of minting.*

VI. WHAT I WOULD WANT A HUMAN TO RE-EXAMINE

Three things, in order of how much they cost if I am wrong.

First, the missing amendment verb. `existence` is the only field on a gap that
asserts an act rather than a judgement, it is the one field no seat can correct,
and its wrong value is invisible downstream. A `regrade --existence` — or a
refusal at mint when `--location` names a heading absent from the live report,
which is the same check the fix-pair already gets — would have made this petition
unnecessary. Blue said the same in its friction and it is right.

Second, whether the bench should be able to reach red at all. I have just issued
a direction I know cannot be delivered. That is a strange thing for a judicial
system to permit, and a human should decide whether relief ought to be threaded
into every seat's prompt rather than blue's alone, and whether petition rulings
ought to render into the transcript the way opinions do.

Third, the run skeleton's silence about its own phase. An empty report and a lost
report are the same bytes here, and I ruled on the charitable reading — that this
was a deliberate pre-motion sitting — partly on the strength of a directory name,
which is precisely the kind of fact this repository's own rules say must never be
recovered from a string. If that reading is wrong, if blue's draft was lost
rather than never written, then red's stamps may have been honest against an
artifact that has since vanished, and the disposition above should be revisited.
I could not tell from the record, and I want a human to know that I could not.

payload.text:
Three capability gaps, all found while ruling on blue's integrity petition, all
verified in the tree at this sitting rather than recalled.

1. NO VERB AMENDS `existence`. I held that R1-1's and R1-2's `existence:
verified` stamps are unsupported, and I could not make the record say so as a
FIELD. `merge regrade` carries severity, likelihood, impact and complexity_cost
and nothing else (tools/internal/cli/merge/regrade.go — the four flag
registrations are the whole set); `blue dispute --dimension` accepts the same
four. So the only axis on a gap that asserts an ACT rather than a judgement is
the only axis nobody can correct, and the correction now lives in my prose while
the field goes on rendering "red checked this defect at the leaf"
(tools/internal/report/assemble.go, existenceNote) to anyone who reads the board
without reading me. That is the exact shape this repo's own facts-are-fields rule
names: the authoritative fact demoted into a document standing in for a record.
What the work wanted: `merge regrade --existence verified|suspected` with a
required reason, on the same footing as the grade axes. Adjacent and cheaper: a
refusal at MINT when `--location` names a heading that is absent from the live
blue/report.md — the fix-pair already gets exactly that forced-re-read treatment
(mint.go calls bluedoc.ValidateProposal against the live report), while
`--location` is free prose validated against nothing, which is why an unfalsifiable
location could be minted three times in one sitting without the tool blinking.

2. GRANTED RELIEF CANNOT REACH RED. My ruling directs red to re-anchor or
restate three locations. I checked whether that direction has a carrier and it
does not. `reliefInEffect` is populated at debate.js:592 and consumed at exactly
one site, debate.js:864 — the BLUE-response prompt. No red prompt receives it.
`petitionLog` (debate.js:591) survives to the capture object at :993 carrying
petitioner, class and ruling only, never the opinion. And a `petition-rule` event
does not render into `--view debate`: the transcript's `### LEAD` block is built
from `opinion` events alone (tools/internal/view/view.go:517-525). So a bench
ruling on a petition ABOUT RED'S CONDUCT is invisible to red through every
channel red is instructed to read. I issued the direction anyway, and said in the
opinion that it does not bind the way blue-facing relief binds, because writing
it as though it bound would be the false receipt. What the work wanted: relief
threaded into every seat's prompt for the round it governs, and petition rulings
rendered into the debate transcript beside the filing they answer.

3. NO DECLARATORY DISPOSITION AT A PETITION SITTING. `bench opinion` requires
`--id <gap>` and an `--as` value that either ends the gap or carries it. I needed
to attach a holding to three gaps WITHOUT disposing of them: blue asked for no
strike and no grade change, no closings have been filed, and ruling the merits at
a petition sitting would exceed the ruling basis my constitution confines me to.
There is no verb for a finding that attaches to a gap and changes nothing about
its fate. The consequence is that the one channel which does render to both seats
(`### LEAD`) was unavailable to me for the one thing I most needed both seats to
see. What the work wanted: either a `bench opinion --as declaratory` that binds
interpretation without moving the gap, or petition rulings rendering in the
transcript, which would have solved this and (2) together.
